guest.bio_context: Bob Frazier is a UC Berkeley computer science graduate who worked as a computer programmer for 15 years before founding a dot-com venture in the mid-1990s that became the largest venture-capitalized company in the Midwest United States with 300 employees, then lost everything in the dot-com crash. He subsequently became a quantitative trader in public markets and experienced a second major loss during the great financial crisis, after which he pivoted to alternative investments and founded Aspen Funds, an alternative investment firm focused on distressed debt and professionally managed portfolios.
